### Session 98f46195-d690-452f-a8c4-47c3ea0f7f84 - 2026-08-14T14:35:45.706Z

- User asked how to implement route-checking (OptimoRoute vs. Google Maps vs. custom app), bulletproof the process with rule validation, create learning loops when defects are found, and what an ideal application architecture would look like.
- Claude Code analyzed next week's board and found a live defect: `territories.json` flags SR-516 with `crossesOwners: false`, but the rulebook says it determines ownership — creating contradictory rules across three files.
- Discovered geocoding coverage gap: 25 of 81 visits on split-boundary zips lack real coordinates and fall back to zip-code guesses; 14 of those decide between Cory and Robert on the SR-516 line, meaning ownership decided by guesswork instead of address location.
- Determined OptimoRoute and Google Maps are not alternatives but complementary: OptimoRoute solves routes and drives the app; Google Geocoding must become Got Moles' own (estimated one-time cost of ~$25 for 5,000 clients).
- Outlined 8 route-checking assertions (tech ownership by date, weekday validity, no weekends, pace-adjusted hours, cadence intervals, coordinate-backed geocoding, no phantom orders, write-freeze compliance) each tied to a past failure.
- Recommended two-part validation: rules linter checking rulebook coherence (zip coverage, owner assignment, tech status, geo-split flag agreement) and golden fixtures with known-correct answers, re-run on every change.
- Proposed a 6-step defect-to-fixture learning loop (capture, adjudicate, fixture, change rules file, re-run all fixtures, log with date and decision) to prevent contradicting prose rules from hiding in the file unseen.
- Described an ideal 5-component system: versioned rules store, pure decision engine with no side effects, fixture suite as regression net, independent verifier with zero-write gate on failure, and run ledger recording before/after values for undo.
- Identified when to outgrow OptimoRoute: when per-driver service-time variance (currently 28% spread measured) makes uniform planning systematically wrong, triggering a solver swap to OR-Tools behind the same interface.
